answers.answer: In 3 players, the tied leaders receive no coin; the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Census: “a tied lead gives no coin” and “In a 2-player game the last player never pays”.

answers.answer: No. Draw at most the allowance (6) and no more than the two free Market spaces permit. Unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Followers: draw up to allowance, “limited by free Market spaces”; unused Market Followers remain.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds; it activates only when all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs only one of two). You cannot execute an incomplete action. A full activation may be saved for a later round. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays on its spaces.

Starting with the Start Player, players go clockwise repeatedly, each taking one activated action or passing. Passing ends your participation for the Action Phase, so you cannot act again that round. An unused activation keeps its Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Actions: “taking one activated action or passing”; passing ends participation; unused activations keep Followers.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives you the good depicted at that track space.

Village chooses one of Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader; the new Follower goes into your bag and its profession track advances one space. Boatman: gain depicted coins, except first at the last space gets a Citizen instead. Craftsman: gain a Technology tile, usable only after you pass. Trader: gain a Place Tile; first advance allows category I only, later advances allow I or II.

The newly recruited Craftsman's Technology cannot help another action that round after you pass; Craftsman-acquired Technology is used only after passing. The first Technology must replace a Farmer. Once placed it cannot move and permanently fills that space; later Technology may replace any profession except Monk; at most one per Place and none at a Place requiring only one Follower.
answers.evidence: Technology placement limits; Village recruitment, Craftsman.

answers.answer: No: the first Trader-track advance allows category I only. Every later advance allows category I or II. Players may inspect the Place Tile stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Setup: players may inspect stacks; Village recruitment, Trader.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and gains its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track; the fourth Knight leaves draw allowance at 7, and the first player to that space takes its Citizen. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. Once a character track is at its last space, you cannot take its corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table, University/Castle/Monastery; Castle rewards; Character-track limits.

answers.answer: Yes. A Monk may replace any profession on an ordinary action. No: a Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. No: substitutions cannot replace the exact professions depicted on Beneficial Deeds.
answers.evidence: Monks; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Ship moves your Merchant along one Waterway (blue) to one adjacent town; Wagon moves along one Road (brown) to one adjacent town. Taking a good is optional; if you collect, take only one, choosing one if two lie there. Empty connections are legal and yield no good.

Guildhall builds one of your Trading Stations in the Merchant's current town, so your Merchant must be there. A town with any player's station cannot receive another. Exception: each player may build one station in Orléans.

Scriptorium gains 1 Development Point by moving one space on the Development Track. On moving onto or past a coin space, collect its depicted coins; first onto/past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; on reaching/passing a Development Status space, Status immediately becomes the shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Scriptorium; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Town Hall activates with one or two neutral Followers of any profession; your four marked starting Followers cannot be used. Send one or both permanently to free Deed spaces matching their exact professions, possibly different Deeds. Take each placement's depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; for Canalization choose 1 coin or 1 Development Point. Whoever fills a Deed's last unoccupied space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Planning; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment in Phase 5 (Actions); it is revealed in Phase 1 and is not resolved in Phase 6. Other normal events resolve in Phase 6. Round 1 opens with Pilgrimage because that tile is placed on top of the shuffled Hour Glass stack.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Setup, Hour Glass; Special Rules & Edge Cases.

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine qualify as food; wool is not food. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. With no food, you owe 5 coins; if you have fewer than five, pay available coins and undergo torture for the shortfall.

A neutral Scholar drawn in Plague returns to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable; its track marker does not move back. A marked starting Trader is kept, so no Follower is lost and no replacement draw is made.

Pay the one coin available; replace each of the two missing coins with one item for each shortfall, choosing from a Trading Station (built or unbuilt), a random eligible Follower from your bag, one Development Point, one Goods Tile, one Place Tile, or one Technology tile. Follower payment is only from your bag; Market/Action Space Followers are ineligible, and marked starting Followers are returned and redrawn until an eligible neutral is drawn. A Development Point moves one space left but never onto or past a coin space. Surrendered items are removed from the game.

You cannot play an action providing an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part would still reward you. It becomes available again when its required tile is available, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply lacks enough coins, players cannot receive coins at that moment.

A tie for most built Trading Stations means nobody takes the bonus Citizen. Grain/cheese/wine/wool/brocade score 1/2/3/4/5 points each. Stations plus collected Citizens score (built stations + Citizens) × final Development Status. Equal scores go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, share victory.

Each player receives a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put those Followers on the Market, Merchant in Orléans, one marker on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track; keep coins and unbuilt stations in front. The youngest player takes the Start Player token.

Set up both shared boards; sort neutral Followers by profession into board buildings, Technology into supply, coins nearby. Put 13 Citizens on marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II. For four players, shuffle goods face down and deal one face up to each eligible Road/Waterway goods space; all such spaces are filled. Sort remaining goods face up into Goods Market.

For 3 players remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders each; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks each; remove 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players remove 4 of each first profession group; 6 of each Knights/Scholars/Monks; remove 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and preceding instruction.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall allows any one or two neutral Followers.
answers.evidence: Actions table; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Yes. For each of the two declined draws, you may instead move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market. You cannot move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
Yes, you may inspect your bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.

The seven phases are Hour Glass reveal, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass the Start Player token left. Planning starts simultaneously; if order matters, plan clockwise from Start Player. Payments and necessary order-sensitive event resolution go clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to the common supply; received coins come from it.
Do not score immediately. Finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including its event; then score.
The uniquely ahead player on the Farmers Track gains 1 Census coin, regardless of Farmer tiles in bags.
answers.evidence: Census compares Farmers Track markers regardless of Farmer tiles in bags.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to current Development Status.
Eight goods means 2 coins (one per complete group of 3, rounded down). Goods types do not matter: Taxes counts all goods. A shortfall causes torture.
You receive 4 coins: Trading Day pays 1 per built Trading Station, and unbuilt reserve stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Trading Day event; only built stations count.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer; 1 grain from Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; 1 cheese from Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; 1 wine from Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; 1 wool from Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; 1 brocade from Goods Market. Each cannot be used when its specific good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table; paragraph following it.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman; gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk; gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman; gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar; gain 2 Development Points.

Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins; each coin advances one Development space, so paying two advances two spaces. Zero is illegal because at least 1 is required; four is illegal because the maximum is 3.
Cellar: Monk + Scholar; gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar; gain 1 coin per built Trading Station. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar; gain coins equal to current Development Status.
Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight. It moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table, Horse Wagon.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile subject to usual placement limits. Your first Technology cannot go on it, because first Technology must replace a Farmer and Laboratory has only Scholar/Craftsman spaces. A later Technology may go on either Laboratory space if none is already there and other limits are met.

Bathhouse requires a Farmer. Draw 3 Followers from your bag, choose 2, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces; neither may go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Farmer to your bag.

Place the one legally placeable drawn Follower immediately on an appropriate Action Space other than Bathhouse. Return the other two drawn Followers and the activating Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse: if only one or none can be legally placed, do so and return all other drawn Followers to bag.

answers.answer: It need not wait until next round. A Place completed during the Action Phase is available on a later action turn in the same phase, provided you have not passed.
Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague.
No. Pilgrimage's no-Monk-recruitment restriction applies during Phase 5 Actions. Sacristy protection is used during Phase 6, so it does not waive the recruitment restriction.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Pilgrimage in Phase 5; Sacristy protection during Phase 6.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not permit replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table, Herb Garden.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It requires no activation. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
No. On Beneficial Deeds, the exact depicted professions are required; substitutions cannot replace them. Gunpowder Tower's Deed option also requires exact types, so it does not change this.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds; Gunpowder Tower table row.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3 place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. During Planning move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, during Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent; Deed spaces still require exact types.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table, Gunpowder Tower.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two tied last players pay nothing.
answers.evidence: Census: tied last place pays nothing.

answers.answer: At the end, before scoring, the unique player with the most built stations receives the set-aside Citizen. That Citizen counts among collected Citizens in final station/Citizen scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring: before scoring, unique most built stations takes Citizen; station/Citizen formula.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 face down, then place that Pilgrimage on top so round 1 has Pilgrimage. In Phase 1 the Start Player reveals the top tile.
Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
Initial Development Status is 1 and initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
Only lost Development Points can be regained. Goods, Followers, stations, Places, and Technology surrendered to torture are removed from the game, not returned to their supplies.
You may choose the order of your actions freely.
The passive substitution ability is available immediately, including in the current Action Phase, as soon as the Place is acquired.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment, Trader: acquired Place and passive special ability available immediately.

answers.answer: You may send just one or both eligible Followers in that Town Hall action.
answers.evidence: Town Hall: send one or both to matching free Deed spaces.

answers.answer: Taking a good is optional; you may complete the move and leave the available good on the connection.
Yes. You may send the second Follower on a later action turn in the same Action Phase before passing; they need not both be transferred in one action.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Town Hall's two Followers may be sent in separate action turns during same Action Phase before passing.
